name: Powdery Mildew
visual_symptoms: white powdery spots on leaves
fuzzy flour-like white coating on leaves stems and buds
white dusty circular patches on foliage
causes: High humidity, low or no airflow, poor ventilation, leaf-on-leaf contact trapping moisture
treatment: Remove affected leaves with wet paper towel. Improve airflow with oscillating and exhaust fans. Spray with 1 part milk to 3 parts water, or potassium bicarbonate (1 tbsp per gallon). For buds: no sprays — improve environment only.
risk_to_consumer: Mold spores can cause respiratory issues. Heavily affected buds should not be consumed.

name: Botrytis (Bud Rot)
visual_symptoms: gray or brown fuzzy mold inside or on buds
sudden yellowing of leaves on large buds within 1-2 days
dark gray or brown rotting bud interior
dusty speckled appearance inside buds
white or gray fuzzy growth at leaf bases
leaves turning purple near infected areas
affected areas easily separate from healthy tissue
causes: Botrytis cinerea fungus. Humidity above 60% RH during flowering, poor airflow, temperatures below 60°F, dense buds with poor air penetration
treatment: Immediately remove and discard ALL affected buds and nearby buds. Do not let infected material contact other areas. Increase airflow, lower humidity below 50%, defoliate dense plants. No sprays work on established bud rot.
risk_to_consumer: CRITICAL — never consume. Botrytis produces mycotoxins that are toxic when inhaled or ingested. All affected buds must be discarded.

name: Leaf Septoria (Yellow Leaf Spot)
visual_symptoms: round yellow or brown spots on lower leaves
spots with darkened borders and small raised center resembling a pimple
circular lesions with tiny dark specks at centers
yellow spots transitioning to brown over time
causes: Fungal or bacterial infection. Spores overwinter in soil and spread via wind and rain.
treatment: Remove all affected leaves carefully. Apply copper-based fungicide or neem oil (avoid buds). Improve air circulation. Keep ground clean of fallen leaves.
risk_to_consumer: Does not directly affect bud safety but indicates poor plant health.

name: Tobacco Mosaic Virus (TMV)
visual_symptoms: uneven stripes of light and dark green on leaves
yellow spots or mottled patterns on foliage
twisted curved or abnormal leaf growth
dark green areas appearing thicker in texture
slow growth and sickly overall appearance
causes: Direct plant-to-plant contact, contaminated hands or tools, tobacco product handling near plants
treatment: No cure — infected plant carries TMV permanently. Remove and isolate affected plants. Enforce strict hand-washing between plant contact. Sanitize all tools.
risk_to_consumer: No known direct risk to consumer but indicates severely compromised plant health and reduced yield quality.

name: Nitrogen Deficiency
visual_symptoms: older lower leaves turning yellow starting from tips
pale green or light-colored foliage throughout plant
yellow leaves turning soft and folding inward before becoming crispy
progressive yellowing from bottom to top of plant
new growth at top remains green
causes: Insufficient nitrogen in medium, root zone pH too low preventing absorption, overwatering limiting uptake
treatment: Apply high-nitrogen nutrients. Adjust pH to 6.0-7.0 for soil. Note: yellowing in late flowering is normal and not a deficiency.
risk_to_consumer: No direct health risk. Indicates lower bud development and cannabinoid density.

name: Nitrogen Toxicity
visual_symptoms: dark green shiny leaves
leaves curling downward at tips in talon-like claw formation
leaves eventually turning yellow or brown and dropping
weak stems and slow growth
causes: Excessive nutrient application, using vegetative nutrients during flowering, hot soils with built-in nutrients, time-release fertilizers
treatment: Reduce nitrogen feeding immediately. Switch to low-nitrogen bloom formula. Flush with pH-balanced water if in nutrient-rich soil.
risk_to_consumer: Excess nitrogen in buds can create harsh unpleasant taste when consumed.

name: Phosphorus Deficiency
visual_symptoms: dark green blue or grayish lower leaves
bronze purple or brown spots and splotches
leaves thickening and curling downward feeling dry or stiff
bright red or purple stems
progressive yellowing before leaves drop
symptoms starting at base and climbing upward
causes: pH imbalance (most common in flowering), poor root health, overwatering, cold temperatures below 60°F, nutrient salt buildup blocking absorption
treatment: Adjust pH: soil 6.2-7.0, hydro 5.5-6.2. Improve root care. Warm root zone to 65-75°F. Flush with pH-balanced water and bloom nutrients.
risk_to_consumer: No direct risk. Indicates underdeveloped buds with lower cannabinoid content.

name: Potassium Deficiency
visual_symptoms: yellow brown or burnt edges and tips on older leaves
yellowing in leaf margins near burnt edges
brown burnt-looking leaf tips appearing pale or bleached
leaf tips curling as edges turn brown
interior leaf veins remaining green
weakened stems
causes: Improper pH levels, overwatering, heat or transplant stress, heavily filtered or RO water lacking minerals
treatment: Adjust pH: soil 6.0-7.0, hydro/coco 5.5-6.5. Flush with pH-balanced water containing standard nutrients.
risk_to_consumer: No direct risk. May indicate lower terpene and cannabinoid density in harvested product.

name: Magnesium Deficiency
visual_symptoms: yellowing between leaf veins while veins remain green (interveinal chlorosis)
yellowing appearing on lower and older leaves first
leaf edges becoming yellow or bright green and crispy
light brown spotting developing as problem worsens
red stems may appear
causes: Incorrect pH (too acidic), calcium-only supplements without magnesium, growing in coco coir or RO water
treatment: Flush with pH-balanced water. Adjust pH to 6.0-7.0 for soil. Apply Cal-Mag supplement or Epsom salt (1 tsp per gallon). Expect improvement within one week.
risk_to_consumer: No direct health risk.

name: Calcium Deficiency
visual_symptoms: brown or bronze splotches or spots on leaves
brown patches on actively growing foliage
slightly purple discoloration especially under LED lights
crinkling mottling and curled leaf tips
stunted or distorted new growth
weak flimsy stems prone to cracking
causes: Low pH at roots, filtered or RO water lacking calcium, hydroponic or coco growing without supplementation, excess potassium blocking absorption
treatment: Flush with pH-balanced water. Adjust pH: soil 6.2-7.0, coco/hydro 6.2-6.5. Apply CaliMagic (1 tsp per gallon). Results visible within one week on new growth.
risk_to_consumer: No direct health risk.

name: Iron Deficiency
visual_symptoms: newest leaves turning bright yellow or white when first emerging
yellowing appearing first on upper inner foliage
damaged yellow leaves may show green recovery starting from tips toward base
in severe cases affected leaves dry up and die
causes: pH too high at root zone (above 7.0 locks out iron), stress conditions, root problems, excessive nutrients causing lockout
treatment: Adjust pH: soil 6.0-6.5, coco/hydro 5.5-6.5. Flush system with clean pH-balanced water. Apply Cal-Mag if deficiency persists. Expect recovery within one week.
risk_to_consumer: No direct health risk.

name: Zinc Deficiency
visual_symptoms: yellowing between veins on younger leaves while veins remain green
leaf tips becoming discolored and dying
unique banded or striped appearance on leaves
vertical growth slowing or stopping
new leaves clustering together with reduced node spacing
buds stopping growth or deteriorating in flowering
causes: pH imbalance (zinc locks out at higher pH), RO water, root problems, overwatering
treatment: Adjust pH: soil 6.0-6.5, hydro 5.5-6.0. Flush with clean pH-adjusted water. Most growers don't need extra zinc — focus on pH correction.
risk_to_consumer: No direct health risk.

name: Nutrient Burn
visual_symptoms: brown or yellow leaf tips and edges
tips turning yellow then tan gold or brown then rusty and crispy
burn spreading inward across leaves in advanced cases
bronze spotting around leaf edges
leaf tips curling upward or downward
dark green overall foliage
causes: Excessive nutrient feeding, high-nutrient soils, wrong nutrient type for growth stage, low light causing reduced nutrient uptake
treatment: Flush with pH-balanced water to remove excess nutrients. Reduce nutrient concentration by half. Do not increase feeding until recovery. Damaged leaves will not recover.
risk_to_consumer: Excess nutrients at harvest creates unpleasant chemical taste. Indicates potential chemical residue in buds.

name: Heat Stress
visual_symptoms: leaves cupping upward into canoe or taco shape
serrated leaf edges flipping upward
yellow or brown spotting with burnt appearance
foxtailing on buds (spire-like growth)
airy underdeveloped bud structure
leaves pointing upward and wilting during extreme heat
causes: Grow lights too close, ambient temperature above 85°F (30°C), low humidity combined with heat, insufficient water, hot water in hydroponic systems
treatment: Raise lights to correct distance. Increase airflow and reduce temperature. Increase watering frequency. Apply seaweed kelp extract for recovery.
risk_to_consumer: Reduces terpene and cannabinoid content. Foxtailed buds have lower potency. No direct safety risk.

name: Light Burn / Bleaching
visual_symptoms: yellow leaves at plant top directly under lights
bleached white or pale yellow patches on upper buds
inner veins remaining green while margins yellow
brown crispy sugar leaves
symptoms concentrated on parts closest to light source
red or purple discoloration instead of yellow in some cases
causes: Grow lights too close to canopy, light intensity too high, extended exposure, high-power LED lights
treatment: Increase distance between lights and canopy. Reduce light intensity. Bleached buds have reduced cannabinoid content — cannot be reversed.
risk_to_consumer: Bleached buds have significantly reduced potency. No safety risk.

name: Windburn
visual_symptoms: clawed or curled leaves forming claw shapes
brown or bronze spots resembling burns
leaf damage confined to areas directly in front of fans
leaves further from fans appear healthy
causes: Fans blowing directly and too strongly onto plants
treatment: Redirect fans to blow at walls not directly on plants. Create gentle circulation — leaves should rustle gently, not wave vigorously.
risk_to_consumer: No health risk.

name: Overwatering
visual_symptoms: leaves drooping and curling downward along entire length soon after watering
leaves feeling firm and puffy not limp
yellowing resembling nutrient deficiencies
stunted growth
very dark green color
soil staying wet for 4-5+ days
causes: Watering too frequently, growing medium retaining too much moisture, containers without drainage holes, roots starved of oxygen
treatment: Allow soil to dry fully between waterings. Improve drainage. Water only when top inch of medium is dry. Increase temperature and airflow to accelerate drying.
risk_to_consumer: No direct health risk but significantly reduces quality and encourages root rot and fungal issues.

name: Underwatering
visual_symptoms: drooping wilting leaves that improve after watering
leaves appearing papery and thin
limp lifeless foliage lacking rigidity
plants perking up noticeably after each watering
yellowing and leaf curling in chronic cases
burnt-looking tips in chronic cases
causes: Inadequate watering frequency or volume, pot-bound conditions, small container size
treatment: Water thoroughly until runoff drains from pot bottom. Water more frequently. Transplant to larger container if rootbound.
risk_to_consumer: No direct health risk. Underdeveloped buds with lower potency.

name: Root Rot
visual_symptoms: wilting despite wet soil
yellowing leaves that don't recover with watering
drooping appearance with curled or cupped leaves
stunted slow growth
overall plant drooping
brown slimy roots if visible
causes: Overwatering, poor drainage, pythium or fusarium fungi, lack of oxygen at roots, warm water temperatures in hydroponic systems
treatment: Identify root cause. Improve drainage, allow medium to dry. Apply beneficial bacteria (Hydroguard, Great White). For hydro: clean reservoir completely. Avoid hydrogen peroxide — it kills beneficial bacteria.
risk_to_consumer: Systemic fungal infection can affect bud quality and safety. May indicate contaminated product.

name: Spider Mites
visual_symptoms: tiny yellow orange or white speckles on leaves (stippling)
fine silk webbing between leaves and buds
leaves turning yellow or bronze from damage
dusty or dirty-looking undersides of leaves
in severe infestations entire buds covered in webbing
causes: Hot dry conditions, low humidity, stagnant air, introduction from infected clones or contaminated tools
treatment: Apply Spinosad (Captain Jack's), insecticidal soap, neem oil, or Grower's Ally spray. Rotate treatments every 2-3 days to prevent resistance. Reduce temperature and increase airflow. Treat at least once after mites appear gone.
risk_to_consumer: Mites and webbing on buds are contaminants. Heavily infested product should not be consumed.

name: Broad Mites
visual_symptoms: twisted drooping new growth at plant top
glossy blistered leaves with wet or plastic-like appearance
leaf edges curling upward
leaves turning yellow bronze or brown before dying
damage concentrated at specific areas with heaviest infestation
flowering buds becoming sickly and dying
causes: Introduction from infected clones or contaminated tools, warm conditions. Too small to see with naked eye.
treatment: Remove infected leaves and stems. Apply neem oil, insecticidal soap, Earth's Ally 3-in-1, or Mite-B-Gone daily for severe cases. Use predatory mites (Neoseiulus). Continue treatment weekly for 5+ weeks after mites appear gone.
risk_to_consumer: Mite contamination on harvested buds is undesirable. Affects taste and safety.

name: Hemp Russet Mites
visual_symptoms: curling of leaf edges
dull-colored brittle leaves
beige or yellow mass at plant tops (the mites themselves)
buds beginning to die with distortions on new growth
plant drooping especially at infestation sites
brown or yellow spots from leaf stress
symptoms worsening toward plant tops
causes: Microscopic mites that lay eggs inside plant tissue. Year-round reproduction. Standard miticides often ineffective.
treatment: Apply neem oil, insecticidal soaps, Mighty Wash, or Avid/Forbid miticide (not during flowering). Use predatory mites. Treat multiple times weekly. Continue for 5 weeks after mites disappear.
risk_to_consumer: Mite infestation on buds reduces quality and safety.

name: Aphids
visual_symptoms: small soft-bodied insects on undersides of leaves and stems
white green yellow black brown or red tiny bugs
yellowing or wilting leaves from excessive feeding
black sooty mold from honeydew deposits
silvery exoskeletons (shed skins) on leaves
causes: Winged colonizer aphids introduce infestation. Warm conditions accelerate reproduction.
treatment: Spray off with pressurized water. Apply insecticidal soap, neem oil, or Spinosad. Control ants which farm aphids. Introduce ladybugs as biological control.
risk_to_consumer: Aphid presence on buds indicates contamination. Affected product should be inspected carefully.

name: Thrips
visual_symptoms: shiny silver or bronze irregular spots on leaves
spots larger and more irregular than spider mite damage
appearance resembling dried spit or tiny snail trails
infested leaves eventually dying if damage persists
pale tubular worm-like nymphs on leaves
causes: Flying insects entering grow space from outdoors or contaminated plants
treatment: Apply insecticidal soap, neem oil, Spinosad, or Pyrethrins (after sunset only — toxic to bees). Sprinkle diatomaceous earth on soil.
risk_to_consumer: Thrip presence on buds is a contaminant concern.

name: Fungus Gnats
visual_symptoms: tiny black or dark brown flies buzzing around soil surface
wilting yellowing or drooping leaves unexplained by other causes
stunted growth or growth cessation
browning spots and leaf curling mimicking nutrient deficiencies
tiny white translucent larvae with black heads in top soil layer
causes: Overwatering is the primary trigger. Warm wet topsoil encourages larvae. Larvae damage roots and spread pathogens.
treatment: Reduce watering — let top inch of soil dry completely between waterings. Place yellow sticky traps. Apply Bacillus thuringiensis (Mosquito Bits) in water, hydrogen peroxide drench (1:4 with water), or Essentria IC3. Without wet topsoil gnats naturally disappear.
risk_to_consumer: Gnats spread pathogens like root rot. Heavily infested plants may have compromised root systems affecting quality.

name: Whiteflies
visual_symptoms: tiny white moth-like insects flying when plant is disturbed
white spots on upper leaf surfaces
leaf discoloration and deterioration
round nymph forms on leaf undersides
eggs practically glued to leaf surface
causes: Entry from outdoors or contaminated plants
treatment: Apply insecticidal soap, neem oil, Spinosad, or Essentria IC3. Thorough coverage of leaf undersides required. Repeat applications needed.
risk_to_consumer: Whitefly infestation on buds is a contaminant. Affects product cleanliness.

name: Mealybugs
visual_symptoms: white hairy fuzzy insects on stems and leaf undersides
white patches resembling mold or webbing
sticky honeydew substance leading to black sooty mold
white powdery or webbing-like patches on leaves and stems
causes: Warm growing environments, poor plant hygiene
treatment: Blast off with pressurized water. Apply insecticidal soap, neem oil, or rubbing alcohol spray (9:1 water to alcohol). Introduce ladybugs. Apply diatomaceous earth to soil.
risk_to_consumer: Mealybug contamination on buds reduces product quality and safety.

name: Leaf Miners
visual_symptoms: pale winding trails or tunnels on leaf surface
pest lives inside leaf tissue creating visible tracks
distinctive tunneling pattern through leaf
causes: Fly larvae tunneling through leaf tissue
treatment: Remove and discard all affected leaves. Apply targeted insecticides for leaf miners.
risk_to_consumer: Primarily affects leaves, rarely reaches buds. Low consumer risk.
